title: Vent a Clothes Dryer: Redirecting a Long Interior Duct to a Short Exterior Run

locations.name: Basement interior (under the dryer)
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly states 'we are in the basement underneath the dryer'

locations.name: Exterior vent termination on exterior wall
locations.basis: Transcript discusses venting directly outside and shows an exterior termination with louvers

summary: This Old House staff assess a dryer vent that runs a long, convoluted path through the basement and out through an exterior wall. They identify lint buildup risks from the maze of ducting and favor rerouting the vent to exit directly outside along the shortest possible path. The process covers drilling a through-wall hole in vinyl siding, installing a 4-inch galvanized elbow and duct, sealing joints with foil tape, and removing the old basement ductwork. The segment also notes the dryer’s lint filter location for ongoing maintenance and demonstrates finishing steps to ensure the new vent path reduces lint accumulation and improves venting efficiency.

sections.title: Basement duct path assessment and problem identification
sections.description: The speaker notes a clogged dryer vent and examines the basement duct layout, highlighting a long path that snakes to the exterior and a design that may trap lint at an elbow. The discussion suggests a need to rethink the route to improve venting performance and reduce lint buildup.

sections.title: Vent-route planning and the case for exterior relocation
sections.description: The plan shifts toward venting directly outside via the shortest straight run. The discussion covers why the existing layout is problematic and considers the most straightforward exterior route from the dryer's original location.

sections.title: Through-wall hole creation and exterior-vent setup
sections.description: A through-wall hole is drilled in vinyl siding using a reverse drill to prevent chipping, then a 4-1/8 inch hole saw is used. A 4-inch galvanized elbow is installed to connect the interior duct to the exterior termination, which features one-directional louvers and an optional critter cover.

sections.title: Final assembly, seal, and lint-filter check
sections.description: The crew seals duct joints with foil tape, removes the old basement duct maze, secures the new run, and notes the lint filter location to complete a ready-to-operate setup and remind the occupant about regular maintenance.

featured_techniques.technique: Reverse drilling to start a hole in vinyl siding without chipping
Cutting through vinyl siding with a hole saw (4-1/8 inch)
Exterior vent termination with directional louvers and optional critter cover
Measuring and fitting galvanized duct to connect to an elbow
Sealing duct joints with foil tape (not duct tape)
Removing existing basement duct maze to simplify the vent path
Locating and inspecting the dryer lint filter for maintenance
